summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose to INR218.5 crore with EBITDA margin of 20.8% and PAT of INR29.4 crore; Q4 revenue INR62.6 crore, up 41.9% YoY.
summary.overview: Mobavenue AI Tech reported Q4 and FY26 results on a call held 18 May 2026 (transcript filed 25 May 2026). Management framed FY26 as its first full year under new leadership, marked by renaming from Lucent Industries, the 100% acquisition of Mobavenue Media Private Limited, and a INR49.99 crore preferential raise. Revenue, EBITDA and PAT each rose sequentially in every quarter of FY26, and revenue per verified outcome climbed from INR44.99 in Q1 to INR48.44 in Q4. Management gave only directional FY27 commentary, anchored on a "Rule of 50" framework (30%+ revenue growth with 20%+ EBITDA margin).

segments.name: International operations
segments.commentary: International revenue was 11.5% of FY26 revenue. UK operations went live during FY26, and LATAM is being set up; the platform serves brands across 10 countries.

segments.name: Direct vs intermediary clients
segments.commentary: Direct clients contributed 73.9% of FY26 revenue, versus reliance on agencies and resellers for the rest.

segments.name: Platform products (GMP 360)
segments.commentary: PrsmX covers awareness (CTV, footfall, brand safety), SurgeX covers mobile user acquisition, DiscoverX and AmplifiX cover OEM and app discovery, and ResurgeX covers re-engagement and retention. Q4 added features completing PrsmX as an omnichannel awareness DSP.

guidance_outlook: FY27 outlook is directional, not formal guidance. Management expects sequential momentum driven by FY26 drivers: international expansion, AI automation, CTV, video streaming and commerce media.
Long-term Rule of 50 framework: sustained annual revenue growth above 30% with EBITDA margin of 20% and above.

FY27 priorities: deepen enterprise and mid-market penetration in India; expand UK and LATAM and evaluate other markets, including selective M&A; scale AI and product innovation through Mobavenue AI Labs.

Management said FY27 growth is in line with organic capability, and M&A will be pursued only for technology or market access. Macro risks (geopolitics, oil prices, inflation) are factored into planning.
capex_capacity: Core decision engine moved from rule-based and traditional ML to a proprietary neural network framework during FY26.
Real-time inference under 15 milliseconds, against an industry benchmark of about 50 milliseconds.
Daily processing of more than 125 crore consented signals, up from 100 crore earlier per the Q&A.
Deep neural networks trained on 50 terabytes of data in about one hour, down from 10 to 12 hours. ML models refresh on near-hourly cycles.
Outcomes delivered: 42.72 million verified outcomes in FY26 across roughly 2.5 billion devices. Headcount exceeded 200 employees.
demand_pricing: Demand strongest in Quick Commerce, Fintech and Retail, per management. Travel was strong in Q1 and Q2 but was hit in Q4 by the post-war slowdown, though domestic travel continues to grow.
Revenue per outcome rose from INR44.99 (Q1) to INR48.44 (Q4), attributed to better monetisation, conversion quality and mix toward premium formats.
Around 80% of revenue comes from retained customers. Active client base is 150+ brands.
Top 10 clients contribute about 25% of revenue and top 50 about 60-65%. Management caps any single client at around 6-7% of revenue.
Brands do not give exclusivity; Mobavenue competes with other programmatic platforms. It positions itself as outcome-based platform rather than agency.

qa_highlights.question: Are acquisitions or strategic partnerships being evaluated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is selective on M&A, looking for technology capability or market and customer access. FY27 growth is expected to be in line with organic capability, and any deal would be priced carefully.

qa_highlights.question: How is the technology platform being strengthened?
qa_highlights.answer: Daily signal processing rose to more than 125 crore from 100 crore earlier. Training time on 50 TB fell to about one hour from 10 to 12 hours, and AI now drives campaign planning and real-time optimisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the customer retention and repeat business trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said retention is strong once clients move beyond pilots. It cited 150 active customers who spend monthly or quarterly, with no quantified churn figure.

qa_highlights.question: Which verticals show the strongest demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Quick Commerce, Fintech and Retail are the top three. Travel was slowed in Q4 by the post-war environment, but domestic travel continues to grow.

qa_highlights.question: What are the 12-24 month strategic priorities?
qa_highlights.answer: Three pillars: deepen enterprise and mid-market penetration in India, global expansion (UK and LATAM over the next 12-18 months, with Asia and other developed markets later), and product and IP innovation through Mobavenue AI Labs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the repeat business share, how do renewals and price increases work, and what is client concentration risk?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80% of revenue comes from retained clients. Pricing improved through higher revenue per outcome, not explicit price-escalation clauses. Top 10 clients are about 25% of revenue and top 50 about 60-65%, with a 6-7% single-client cap.

risks_watch: Quick Commerce and Commerce clients carry higher concentration and may breach the 6-7% single-client cap; management is widening platform use to diversify.
Travel demand softened in Q4 after the post-war environment; management cites geopolitics, oil-price volatility and inflation as macro risks.
Employee costs grew 26.1% QoQ in Q4, and PAT margin dipped to 13.5% in Q4 from 13.4% for the full year.
Supply and data costs are about 60% of revenue; margin depends on sustaining revenue per outcome gains.
Further M&A and international expansion (UK, LATAM) could absorb capital raised in the INR49.99 crore preferential issue.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY26 execution and sequential growth, with management describing the results as disciplined, not a single-quarter outcome. Guidance is deliberately soft ("directional, not formal"), and management was evasive on quantified retention, repeat-business share and M&A pipeline. Multiple audio-quality interruptions during the Q&A left some answers only partly addressed.
key_quotes: Our long-term operating philosophy continues to be anchored around what we call, and we introduced in the last call as Rule of 50, targeting a sustained annual revenue growth of over 30% along with EBITDA margin profile of 20% and above.
Our outlook for FY27 remains directional rather than formal guidance for us, consistent with our earlier communication too.
Owning all three layers, meaning every signal improves our prediction, every prediction improves our outcome, every outcome improves our next signal.
